The stop is a real clash with main's guard. With the merge applied, `wire_post::a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects` fails, because main's wire laws now judge the skim passes this PR adds and block the post:

`post blocked - Punch1: wire gouge: the kerf of move 8 enters the part by 0.0200 mm near X-20.000 Y0.000 at Z0.001 (14 move(s) gouge)`

So either the skim offsets (smaller offset than the rough pass) put the kerf 0.02 mm into the part under the law's model, or the law's kerf model does not know skim offsets. That decision (and the golden `wire_contour_punch_skims.nc`, which would not post today) is the author's, so I did not touch logic or regenerate the golden. Please merge main, decide how the skim passes satisfy the wire gouge law, and re-gate.
taken by UMA for the skim/gouge-law decision @ 9cea9fe

Skim/gouge-law decision (UMA) @ f3e11d1

**Verdict: (b). Main's wire law judged every move with the rough pass's kerf; the skim offsets are right.**

The test's conditions (wire Ø0.25, so r = 0.125; punch, part's left side at X-20):
- rough C110: gap 0.04, offset 0.165 (X-20.165)
- skim 1 S21: gap 0.02, offset 0.145 (X-20.145)
- skim 2 S31: gap 0.01, offset 0.135 (X-20.135)

The rough pass is moves 1-7, so move 8 is skim 1's lead-in to X-20.145 Y0. Main's `wire_verify` handed the law one half-width, 0.125 + 0.04 = 0.165, for every move. Measured that way, move 8 enters by 0.165 - 0.145 = **0.0200 mm**, exactly the reported finding. Each pass really burns only its own r + g, so every pass's kerf edge, the last skim's included, sits on the outline (0.145 - 0.145 = 0 and 0.135 - 0.135 = 0). The last skim sets the finished size, and the 0.03 mm between the rough and the last skim is the stock the skims remove.

**Fix (b), with the law kept conservative.** `WireJob.skim_offsets` carries each skim's own r + g, read from the same condition table the generator uses. The new `sim/src/verify/wire/passes.rs` splits the path at each return to the threading point (the rule `announce_skims` already uses) and judges each move at its own pass's half-width. That half-width is the real kerf of that pass, never narrower. The threading law takes the widest pass's kerf, and the slug law sweeps each pass at its own offset and joins the results. If the path does not return once per stated pass, or an open run states skims, the law refuses it by name. Skims on an open run are also refused at the door (`check_passes`). The arithmetic is in `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md`.

Pinned by `sim verify::wire::tests::each_pass_is_judged_at_its_own_kerf`. That test shows the path is clean at its own kerf, that the single-offset reading reproduces the false gouge at move 8 with depth K - ks, and that a skim 0.05 mm too near is still a 0.05 mm gouge at move 8. Also pinned by `passes_that_cannot_be_told_apart_are_unreadable`, motion `skim_laws_refuse_by_name` (open run), and `wire_post::a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects`, which now posts through the gate. Golden `wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` is **unchanged** (byte-identical).
